title: TUI: preserve bounded stderr diagnostics from failed sandbox commands
scenario: Run each revision's real DockerSandbox.execute implementation against a mocked failed compiler process with 200 stdout characters, `fatal compiler error` on stderr, exit code 1, and an 80-character cap. Serialize the result through the corresponding gate event shape, replay it through the real TUI, open Round 1, and zoom the transcript.

before.observed: The retained stdout prefix is followed by `...[truncated, 141 bytes omitted]`; the fatal stderr diagnostic is absent.

after.observed: The bounded stdout prefix and in-cap marker remain, followed by the retained `fatal compiler error` stderr tail.

assertions: Before renders `bytes omitted` and does not render `fatal compiler error`.
commands: tui-test run --backend alacritty --cols 160 --rows 45 clients/tui/dev/mock-ui.sh --fixture FIXTURE --speed 0 --theme dark
tui-test key press Enter; tui-test key press Enter; tui-test key press F4
limitations: The subprocess call is mocked, so Docker access is unnecessary. The sandbox truncation and returned result are produced by each revision's unmodified DockerSandbox.execute code; the temporary generator only supplies subprocess.CompletedProcess and wraps the returned fields in a minimal valid run replay. The still image demonstrates retained diagnostic content, not Docker or Modal integration. PNGs are static CairoSVG exports of tui-test's settled SVG capture; the original SVGs are included.
